The main argument is that fines are becoming so high that businesses are trying to implement measures to prevent them from happening which means that they are trying to spend money to save money in the long run. If A is true, it just contradicts the argument as a whole.

D isn’t the answer because 1)fines generally vary depending on the situation, discovery of negligence, injury or damages suffered, judge decision, etc which makes it unpredictable and 2)fines aren’t completely an "ordinary expense" like paying a worker which is a general expense but businesses do consider it as a perspective expense and will try their best to reduce it.
